        {"n": 1, "text": "hari; not, as might be supposed from the name, the celebrated", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 2, "text": "brother of Vikramâditya, but a grammarian and poet who was son", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 3, "text": "of S'rîdharasvâmî (sic; sed vide supra) as we are informed by", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 4, "text": "one of his scholiasts, Vidyâvinoda.”[*] In his Oxford catalogue,", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 5, "text": "", "end": "join"},
        {"n": 6, "text": "Prof. Aufrecht speaks of Bhartṛihari, “cujus liber grammaticus", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 7, "text": "minime vero Bhaṭṭikâvyam memoratur”.[†] Dr. Bhâu says that Bhaṭṭi", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 8, "text": "“is popularly believed to have been a son of Bhartṛihari.”[‡]", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 9, "text": "", "end": "join"},
        {"n": 10, "text": "Bohlen says: “They say that Vikrama in fact got possession of", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 11, "text": "the kingdom, and took to himself Bhaṭṭi as Prime Minister.", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 12, "text": "But in this again they seem to have gone wrong, con-", "end": "hyphen"},
        {"n": 13, "text": "founding both persons and times. For there exists a grammati-", "end": "hyphen"},
        {"n": 14, "text": "cal poem called Bhaṭṭikâvya, describing at the same time the ex-", "end": "hyphen"},
        {"n": 15, "text": "ploits of Râma, which has been attributed to a certain gram-", "end": "hyphen"},
        {"n": 16, "text": "marian belonging to a later age called Bhartṛihari, and from the", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 17, "text": "name of this poem, I think, Bhaṭṭi seems to have been considered", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 18, "text": "as the brother of this our Bhartṛihari.”[§] Lastly, Mr. Sashagiri", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 19, "text": "", "end": "join"},
        {"n": 20, "text": "S'âstrî says “King Vikramâditya is said to have been the son of", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 21, "text": "a Brâhmaṇ named Chandragupta who married four wives, one of", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 22, "text": "the Brâhmaṇ caste, another of the Kshatriya, the third of the", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 23, "text": "Vais'ya, the fourth of the S'ûdra caste. They were called Brâh-", "end": "hyphen"},
        {"n": 24, "text": "maṇî, Bhânumatî, Bhâgyavatî, and Sindhumatî. Each of the", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 25, "text": "", "end": "join"},
        {"n": 26, "text": "four bore him a son. Vararuchi was born of the first wife,", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 27, "text": "Vikramârka of the second, Bhaṭṭi of the third, and Bhartṛihari", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 28, "text": "of the fourth. Vikramârka became king, while Bhaṭṭi served", "end": "space"},
        {"n": 29, "text": "him in the capacity of Prime Minister.”[¶] From this conspectus of", "end": "space"}
      ],
      "uncertain": false,
      "note": null
    },
